images.seen: A grinning man filming a giant lightning strike on his phone from the bedroom window, the suburb lit below. Sunday.
lines: Every South African storm gets filmed vertical, and this one earned it.
The strike lasted half a second; the video will last the whole group chat.
The sky does one take and expects you to be ready.

images.seen: A runner in black kit standing in the road with hands on hips, glaring up at a heavy grey storm sky before his run, stone house behind. Saturday.
lines: Warm-up done; now he is waiting on a ruling from upstairs.
The sky is loading something and the question is whether it lands mid-run.
Hands on hips: the international sign for arguing with weather.

images.seen: A woman in a gown with her coffee on the porch at dawn, watching twin pink lightning strikes over the mountains, wet street below. Sunday.
lines: The storm is keeping to the mountains, and the stoep is keeping the view.
First coffee of the day, best show of the week, same ten minutes.
The rain has been and gone; the electricity is still saying goodbye.

images.seen: A bakkie driving away down a red dirt road between mealie fields, dust glowing in the last light under an orange storm-lit horizon. Friday.
lines: That horizon is half sunset, half warning, and the bakkie knows the difference.
Dust now, mud by dark — that cloud bank is not decoration.
The mealies have been waiting for that cloud longer than anyone in the bakkie.
